newsitem.title: USA: Two U.S. independent power lobby groups to merge.
newsitem.headline: Two U.S. independent power lobby groups to merge.

text.p: Two U.S. independent power producer lobbying groups, the Electric Generation Association and National Independent Energy Producers, said on Monday they planned to merge by the end of the year.

EGA, which largely represents independent power affiliates of utilities, and NIEP, which mainly represents small independent power producers, were set to announce the merger and the name of the new group on December 3.
Officials at both organizations said it made sense to join forces to forge a stronger, unified voice in the debate over the opening of electricity markets to competition.
"As the industry has restructured, a lot of the differences that separated us based on where our centers of gravity were have narrowed," said Tobyn Anderson, NIEP's director of legislative affairs.
"It'll eliminate any confusion about where the independent power industry stands," said Anderson, who will keep the same title in the merged group.

The new group is seeking an executive director and plans no lay-offs. The combined staff is expected to number 12, with a few people from both groups not planning to join the merged association, Anderson said.
